actions.mechanism: A customer round-robin ring bounds dispatch opportunities independently of estimated runtime or mean latency.
actions.implementation: On worker release, dispatch the head customer's oldest job; append still-backlogged customers and newly active customers at the tail.
actions.check: With N customers present when a customer joins the tail, verify service within N dispatches. Report mean latency separately.
actions.risk: Dispatch fairness does not imply equal worker-seconds; running transforms remain nonpreemptible.

actions.mechanism: Alternate guaranteed customer turns with globally shortest-estimated-job dispatches, preserving progress regardless of estimation errors.
actions.implementation: Maintain one global alternation bit. Bonus dispatches must not move a still-backlogged customer backward in the fairness ring.
actions.check: Verify each waiting customer receives a guaranteed turn within 2N total dispatches, and oldest long jobs continue starting.
actions.risk: Twelve running long transforms can still delay every short job until a worker finishes.

actions.mechanism: Observed prediction errors adjust bonus-job rankings; guaranteed turns never depend on prediction accuracy.
actions.implementation: Store the last 100 completed runtimes with original estimates and completion times. Apply their median actual-to-estimated ratio to customer estimates.
actions.check: Compare corrected and original prediction errors on subsequent completions; disable correction if errors worsen. Preserve raw residuals for inspection.
actions.risk: Sparse or stale histories and changing workloads can make corrections misleading.

actions.mechanism: An event-driven twelve-worker simulation separates bounded customer progress from improvements in short-job latency.
actions.implementation: Continuously replenish one customer's sixty-second jobs; inject occasional one-second jobs from others. Test accurate, inverted, and stale estimates.
actions.check: Assert dispatch bounds and continued long-job starts; compare short-job p95 waiting time and overall mean latency against FIFO.
actions.risk: Simulation results depend on arrival assumptions; repeat with production traces before claiming gains.
